decisions.feature_outline_summary: [KILL] Data Sovereignty & Offline-First: Users demand local data storage, offline access, and full data portability. Connectivity dependency is a churn trigger, not a feature gap.. This direction conflicts with constitutional constraints.

violated_clauses.clause_text: cloud-only storage with no local option
violated_clauses.violation_reason: Theme content matches forbidden clause "cloud-only storage with no local option" (matched: cloud-only, storage, local)

supporting_evidence.raw_text: I switched from Notion because I got tired of my notes being in someone else's cloud. I need to own my data. Period.
The offline thing is huge for me. I travel a lot, I'm on planes, I can't depend on cloud. If it doesn't work offline, I don't use it.
Feature: offline_sync — 78% of active users enable offline mode within first week. Retention for offline-enabled users: 85% at D30 vs 45% for cloud-only users.
Love the concept but the app is useless without internet. I was on a flight and couldn't access my notes. Deleted it.
I love that my data stays on my device. This is how all productivity tools should work. Take my money.
I exported my data as CSV but it doesn't include my tags or folder structure. The export is useless without metadata. I feel trapped.

decisions.kill_reason: Violates 1 constitutional clause(s): cloud-only storage with no local option

decisions.feature_outline_summary: [BUILD] Judgment Bottleneck at Scale: AI-accelerated production has created a decision backlog. Teams with 15+ candidates cannot allocate resources effectively using spreadsheets and intuition.. Aligned with constitutional direction and supported by customer evidence.

supporting_evidence.raw_text: We evaluated 8 tools last quarter. Shipped features for 6 of them. Two actually moved metrics. The other 4 were a waste. We had no framework to say no earlier.
AI coding tools let us prototype in hours. But now we have 15 prototypes and no idea which 3 to actually invest in. The decision backlog is worse than the dev backlog ever was.
We use Notion + a spreadsheet + gut feeling. It works okay for 10 candidates. But we now have 40 and the spreadsheet is chaos. I need something that scales beyond gut.
Shipped 3 features this week with Cursor. None of them were in our roadmap. We just... built what felt exciting. Now I'm not sure any of them matter.
I'd pay $200/month if it could tell me which of our 20 feature candidates to kill, with evidence I can show to stakeholders. Right now I spend a full week every quarter on prioritization theater.

decisions.build_rationale: Aligns with 1 clause(s) and supported by 3 critical observations. Theme aligns with "simplicity and minimalism; fewer features done well over feature bloat" (matched: features, feature)

decisions.feature_outline_summary: [DEFER] Kill Decision Accountability: PMs need evidence-based kill justification to survive executive scrutiny. 'Gut feeling' is politically indefensible; clause-level reasoning provides organizational cover.. Revisit when more evidence supports prioritization.

supporting_evidence.raw_text: We don't need another AI that tells us what to build. We need something that helps us explain why we're NOT building something. My CEO keeps asking 'why did we kill that?' and I can't point to anything concrete.

What I really want is a way to explain to my CEO why we killed something. Not 'I felt it wasn't right' but 'here are 12 pieces of evidence and 2 constitutional violations'. That's what gets me political cover.
Our PM team of 5 each has their own prioritization spreadsheet. When we need to decide what to cut, it becomes political. There's no shared framework.
The kill board is brilliant. Never seen another tool that shows you what NOT to build with actual evidence. This is what product management has been missing.
Show me the evidence trail. If I can click on a kill decision and see the exact customer quotes that led to it, that's worth the subscription alone.

decisions.defer_reason: Insufficient evidence to decide. 5 observations evaluated, no strong constitutional signal.

supporting_evidence.raw_text: Feature: social_activity_feed — only 12% of users interact with it. Of those, 60% disable it within 2 weeks. Top complaint in settings: 'too noisy'.
Feature: ai_suggestion_panel — 45% click-through on first exposure, drops to 8% by day 7. Users who disable it have higher D30 retention (72%) than users who keep it (58%).
The AI features feel forced. I didn't ask for suggestions while writing. It breaks my flow. Let me turn them off or I'm leaving.
Notification spam killed it for me. I turned off notifications and forgot the app existed. Engagement tricks don't work on people who want focus.
Feature: gamification_badges — 5% adoption after 30 days. Users who interact with badges have 20% lower NPS than non-interactors. Negative correlation with focus_mode usage.
Feature: notification_digest — sent daily to 100% of users. Open rate: 8%. Click-through: 2%. Unsubscribe requests: 340 in past month (12% of MAU).

decisions.kill_reason: Violates 3 constitutional clause(s): data monetization, advertising, engagement-maximizing dark patterns; notification spam to drive engagement; social features that expose user activity

supporting_evidence.raw_text: I want my team to collaborate in real-time. Async is too slow for us. We need everyone seeing the same board, same data, same decisions, live.
Feature: team_dashboard — 92% of teams with 3+ members use it daily. Correlates with 2.3x higher expansion revenue. Top request: 'make the kill/defer reasons visible to the whole team'.
Feature: real_time_collab — 88% adoption in teams >5 people. Average session overlap: 3.2 concurrent users. But solo founders never use it (0% adoption for team_size=1).
Great for solo use but terrible for teams. Can't share a board, can't see what others decided. We need team visibility.
Tried to use this for my team of 8. The lack of role-based access is a non-starter. I can't have junior PMs overriding kill decisions made by the Head of Product.

This replaced our quarterly planning. We used to spend 2 weeks in meetings deciding what to build. Now it takes 2 hours with BONSAI and the decisions are better because they're evidence-based.

decisions.defer_reason: No strong constitutional alignment found and urgency is medium. Evidence is insufficient to prioritize.

decisions.feature_outline_summary: [DEFER] Constitution Usability & Trust: Constitution is the core differentiator but also the biggest onboarding barrier. Writing 3 lines takes 45 min. Normalization errors destroy trust. Parser accuracy is existential.. Revisit when more evidence supports prioritization.

supporting_evidence.raw_text: Onboarding funnel: signup (100%) → constitution_input (68%) → first_pipeline_run (41%) → evidence_drilldown (22%) → execution_packet (9%). Biggest drop: constitution_input → first_pipeline_run.
The kill reasoning said 'violates prohibited_business_model' but my constitution says 'we never compromise on quality'. That's not a business model violation. The clause mapping is wrong.

I tried explaining the 'constitution' concept to my team and they looked at me like I was crazy. The naming is too academic. Just call it 'product policy' or 'team principles'.
